ap_microeconomics-f01.title: A market with a price ceiling

stimulus.description: Quantity demanded and quantity supplied of concert tickets at different prices in a competitive market.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the competitive market for concert tickets. On your graph, label the equilibrium price (P_E) and the equilibrium quantity (Q_E).
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. A downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve with Price and Quantity axes, intersecting at P_E and Q_E.

required_elements: Draws a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve with Price and Quantity labeled on the axes and the curves labeled
alt_solutions: curves may be labeled D and S
axes may be labeled P and Q
common_errors: draws two curves with the same slope sign
omits an axis label
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels the intersection of the curves as the equilibrium with P_E on the price axis and Q_E on the quantity axis
alt_solutions: drops dashed lines from the intersection to the axes
labels the equilibrium point E with P_E and Q_E
common_errors: labels a point that is not the intersection
labels only the price
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Using the table, determine the equilibrium quantity.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied at $10, where 100 units are traded.

required_elements: Identifies the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and reads the quantity (the quantity answer is correct)
alt_solutions: the row where the two quantities are equal
equilibrium quantity from the table
common_errors: reports the equilibrium price instead of the quantity
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The government sets a price ceiling of $7 per unit. On your graph, show the price ceiling, label the quantity actually traded (Q_C), and label the shortage.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. A horizontal line at the ceiling below P_E, Q_C on the quantity axis at the quantity supplied at the ceiling, and the horizontal gap between supply and demand at the ceiling labeled as the shortage.

required_elements: Draws a horizontal price ceiling line below the equilibrium price and labels it with the ceiling price
alt_solutions: the line may extend across the graph at the ceiling price
the line is labeled price ceiling or PC
common_errors: draws the ceiling above the equilibrium price
draws a vertical line
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels Q_C where the ceiling meets the supply curve and marks the gap between the supply and demand curves at the ceiling as the shortage
alt_solutions: Q_C is marked on the horizontal axis at the quantity supplied
the shortage is shown as a horizontal segment between supply and demand
common_errors: marks Q_C at the quantity demanded
labels the surplus instead of the shortage
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Using the table, calculate the quantity demanded and the quantity supplied at the price ceiling and the size of the shortage.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. At $7: quantity demanded is 115 and quantity supplied is 88, so the shortage is 27 units.

required_elements: Reads the quantity demanded and quantity supplied at the ceiling price (both answers are correct)
alt_solutions: row of the table at the ceiling price
quantity demanded and supplied at the ceiling
common_errors: reads quantities at the equilibrium price
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Subtracts quantity supplied from quantity demanded to find the shortage (the shortage answer is correct)
alt_solutions: difference between demanded and supplied
excess of quantity demanded over quantity supplied
common_errors: reports the quantity traded as the shortage
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Explain why the price ceiling creates a deadweight loss.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The quantity traded falls below the efficient quantity, so some transactions in which the buyer's value exceeds the seller's cost do not occur, which lowers total surplus and creates a deadweight loss.

required_elements: States that the quantity traded under the ceiling is less than the equilibrium (efficient) quantity
alt_solutions: fewer units are bought and sold than at equilibrium
the quantity traded is limited by the quantity supplied at the ceiling
common_errors: says the quantity traded rises
says the quantity traded equals the quantity demanded
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains the lost mutually beneficial trades
required_elements: Explains that some transactions in which buyers value the good above its cost of production do not occur, so total surplus falls (the deadweight loss)
alt_solutions: trades where willingness to pay exceeds the cost are lost
total surplus is lower than at the equilibrium
common_errors: says total surplus rises
says producers gain more than consumers lose
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: F
parts.prompt: Suppose instead the government had set a price ceiling of $13 per unit. Identify what would happen to the quantity traded and explain why.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The quantity traded would not change, because $13 is above the equilibrium price of $10, so the ceiling is not binding.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the ceiling is nonbinding and gives the reason
required_elements: States that the quantity traded would be unchanged because a ceiling above the equilibrium price is not binding
alt_solutions: no effect on price or quantity
the market stays at equilibrium
common_errors: says a shortage would arise
says the quantity traded would fall
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

draws MR and demand with the same slope

ap_microeconomics-f05.title: A market with a negative externality

stimulus.description: Marginal private benefit, marginal private cost, and marginal external cost per unit in the market for chemical dyes.

notes: Production of chemical dyes imposes a constant external cost of $40 per unit on people who are not buyers or sellers.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the market for chemical dyes showing demand, private supply, and marginal social cost. Label the market quantity (Q_M) and the socially efficient quantity (Q_E).
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Demand and upward-sloping supply, with the MSC curve above supply; Q_M where demand meets supply and Q_E, smaller, where demand meets MSC.

required_elements: Draws a downward-sloping demand curve, an upward-sloping private supply curve, and a marginal social cost curve above the supply curve, all labeled, with Price and Quantity on the axes
alt_solutions: MSC may be labeled MSC or social cost
supply may be labeled S or private cost
common_errors: draws MSC below supply
omits the MSC curve
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels Q_M where demand meets supply and Q_E where demand meets the marginal social cost curve, with Q_E less than Q_M
alt_solutions: dashed lines to the horizontal axis at each intersection
Q_E drawn to the left of Q_M
common_errors: labels Q_E to the right of Q_M
labels both quantities at the same point
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain why the market quantity is greater than the efficient quantity.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Producers ignore the external cost, so the market supply curve reflects only private cost and the market produces where marginal private benefit equals marginal private cost, beyond the point where marginal social cost equals benefit.

required_elements: Explains that producers do not bear the external cost, so the market produces beyond the point where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost
alt_solutions: private cost is below social cost
the market ignores the cost imposed on third parties
common_errors: says the market underproduces
says producers pay the external cost
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the per-unit tax that would lead the market to produce the efficient quantity.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. A tax equal to the marginal external cost, $40 per unit.

required_elements: Sets the per-unit tax equal to the marginal external cost (the tax answer is correct)
alt_solutions: tax equals the external cost per unit
a Pigouvian tax
common_errors: reports the market price
reports the total external cost
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Suppose the government instead gives producers of chemical dyes a per-unit subsidy. Would the quantity produced move closer to or farther from the efficient quantity? Explain.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Farther from the efficient quantity, because the subsidy shifts private supply right and increases a quantity that is already too large.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains the effect of the subsidy
required_elements: States that the quantity moves farther from the efficient quantity because a subsidy lowers private cost and raises an already excessive quantity
alt_solutions: the market would overproduce even more
supply shifts right and output increases
common_errors: says the subsidy moves output closer to Q_E
says the subsidy reduces output
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.
